source_text: Ἐγέλα ποτὲ πλατὺν κατὰ τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης φύσεως ὁ διάβολος γέλωτα, καὶ ταῖς συμφοραῖς ἡμῶν ἑορταῖς ἐπευφραίνεται. Ἀλλ' ὁ μὲν γέλως τριήμερος· ὁ δὲ θρῆνος αἰώνιος· καὶ πλατὺς γέλως θρῆνον αὐτῷ πλατύτερον κατεσκεύασεν, δάκρυον ἀδιάλειπτον, κλαυθμὸν ἀπαρηγόρητον· βέλος ἐγκάρδιον. Τοῦτο τὸ βέλος ἐν τῇ παρθενικῇ καμίνῳ, οἷον ἠθέλησεν, καὶ ὡς ἠθέλησεν, διὰ πυρὸς κατὰ τοῦ ἐχθροῦ ὁ πολεμάρχης ἐχάλκευσεν· καὶ στομώσας τῇ ἐνεργείᾳ τῆς ἀηττήτου θεότητος, καὶ βάψας τῷ ὕδατι τοῦ ἀχράντου βαπτίσματος, καὶ ἀκονήσας τοῖς ἀπαθέσι παθήμασιν, καὶ στιλβώσας διὰ τῆς μυστικῆς ἀναστάσεως· δι' ἑαυτοῦ πανστρατιᾷ τὸν ἀλάστορα ἐθανάτωσε. Ποῖος οὖν λόγος ἢ τὴν ἡμετέραν χαρὰν ἢ τὴν ἐκείνου συμφορὰν διηγήσηται; Ὁ γὰρ ποτὲ ἀρχάγγελος, νῦν διάβολος· ὁ ποτὲ ἐν οὐρανοῖς διαιτώμενος, νῦν ὡς ὄφις ἐπὶ γῆς θεωρεῖται συρόμενος· ὁ ποτὲ μετὰ τῶν χερουβὶμ ἀγαλλόμενος, νῦν ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ τῶν χοίρων ἐγκέκλεισται ὀδυνόμενος· ὅνπερ τροπωσόμεθα ἐναντία τῆς ἐκείνου φρονήσαντες προαιρέσεως· χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The devil's laughter turned to eternal mourning by Christ's victory
orientation: The speaker contrasts the devil's former broad laughter at human misfortunes with his current eternal lament, showing how Christ forged a deadly weapon in the virgin's womb and destroyed the enemy through his own human nature.
pass_a_gloss: The devil once laughed a broad laugh against human nature, and he rejoices in our misfortunes as festivals. But the laughter is three-day; but the lament is eternal; and a broad laugh prepared for him a broader lament, an unceasing tear, an unappeasable weeping, a heart-piercing missile. This missile in the virginal furnace, as he wished and how he wished, the commander forged through fire against the enemy; and having sheathed it with the working of the unvanquished divinity, and having dipped it in the water of the unblemished baptism, and having whetted it with the impassible passions, and having made it shine through the mystical resurrection; through himself he put to death the unappeasable enemy with all his host. What word then will narrate either our joy or his misfortune? For the once archangel, now devil; the once dwelling in heavens, now like a serpent is seen dragging on earth; the once exulting with the cherubim, now in the prison of the swine is shut up grieving; whom we will turn against by thinking contrary purposes to his purpose; by grace and philanthropy of our Lord Jesus Christ; to whom the glory and the dominion into the ages of the ages, Amen.

lemmas.gloss: rejoices in, makes merry at (present middle/passive indicative, 3rd sg.)
three-day, lasting three days (nominative sg. masculine)
heart-piercing, in the heart (accusative sg. neuter)

choices.why: Glossary bans personified 'Death'; 'broad' captures the spatial metaphor of the devil's expansive mockery
Metaphor for the Virgin's womb where Christ's humanity was forged; 'furnace' retains the metallurgical imagery
Christ as divine war-leader forging the weapon; 'commander' is literal for polemarchos

choices.gloss: having sheathed, having furnished with a mouth/edge (aorist active participle, nominative sg. masculine)

choices.english: having sheathed it with the working
choices.why: Stomoo implies putting a mouth/edge on a weapon; 'sheathed' captures the metallurgical sense of fitting the blade
Technical theological phrase: Christ's voluntary sufferings in an impassible nature; 'impassible' matches glossary sense for apathes
Alastor denotes a blood-feud spirit that cannot be appeased; fits the devil's eternal enmity

choices.english: in the prison of the swine
choices.why: Alludes to the Gadarene demons entering swine (Mark 5:11-13); 'swine' is literal for choiron

bible_refs.note: Implied taunt structure 'Where, O death...' reversed: devil's laughter becomes eternal lament
Demons enter herd of swine; here devil confined in 'prison of the swine'
Fall of morning star from heaven; 'once archangel, now devil... dragging on earth like a serpent'
Satan fell like lightning from heaven; parallels 'once dwelling in heavens, now like a serpent dragging on earth'

pass_b_english: The devil once let out a broad laugh against human nature, and he made merry at our misfortunes as if they were feasts. But his laughter lasted three days, while the lament is eternal; a broader laughter prepared for him a wider lament, a ceaseless tear, an unending wail, a heart-piercing missile. The commander forged this missile in the virginal furnace, as he willed and when he willed, hammering it against the enemy through fire; he gave it its edge by the working of the unconquerable Godhead, tempered it in the water of the spotless baptism, sharpened it with the impassible passions, and made it gleam through the mystical resurrection. Through himself he killed the unappeasable enemy with all his host. What word could recount either our joy or his calamity? The one who was once an archangel is now the devil; the one who once dwelt in the heavens is now seen dragging on the earth like a serpent; the one who once rejoiced with the cherubim is now shut in the prison of the swine, in anguish. We shall turn him back by thinking the opposite of his purpose, by the grace and philanthropy of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: he sheathed it with the working of the unconquerable Godhead
problems.source_quote: στομώσας τῇ ἐνεργείᾳ τῆς ἀηττήτου θεότητος
problems.why: στομόω means to give a blade a hard edge or temper it. 'Sheathed' means covering it, which is the opposite idea and breaks the smithing sequence.
problems.fix: he gave it its edge by the working of the unconquerable Godhead

edits.old: he sheathed it with the working of the unconquerable Godhead
edits.new: he gave it its edge by the working of the unconquerable Godhead

fixed: Fixed `sheathed' -> `gave it its edge': στομώσας means giving a blade its edge/temper, not covering it, fitting the forging sequence.
